memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "they invaded all Egypt and settled down in every area of the country in great numbers. Never before had there been such a plague of locusts, nor will there ever be again. They covered all the ground until it was black. They devoured all that was left after the hail—everything growing in the fields and the fruit on the trees. Nothing green remained on tree or plant in all the land of Egypt." - Exodus 10:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The land goes black. Then nothing green remains. Egypt, the breadbasket of the ancient world, is stripped bare in a day.

This is total loss, and Scripture does not dress it up. Real farmers lost real harvests. Real families faced hunger. Judgement is not tidy.

But hold this beside a promise God made through the prophet Joel to a later generation who had also seen locusts strip their land. God said He would repay them for the years the locusts had eaten (Joel 2:25). The God who sends judgement is also the God who restores.

We should be careful — that promise was spoken to Israel in a particular moment, and it is not a guarantee that every lost year will be replaced in this life. But it does reveal God's heart. He is a restorer by nature.

If you are looking at a season that feels stripped bare — of health, of relationship, of opportunity — bring it to the God who specialises in making things grow again.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What season of my life feels stripped bare?
2. Do I believe God is by nature a restorer?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You see the barren places in my life. I bring them to You, trusting Your heart to restore. Amen.
